# Register of commitments

This register lists everything the theory assumes, defines, or leaves open, one entry per item.
Each later paper adds its own entries in a new layer and cites the register for what it builds on.
A result in any layer should be traceable, through the **Requires** fields, to the entries it rests on.

The register is generated from the entries in `organon/graph/mec/` (one file per entry) and
`organon/method/`; the entry with id X is in the file `X.md` there.

**Entry kinds.**
*Premise*: the starting point that motivates the commitments.
*Commitment*: admitted, not derived; each must be argued for where it is introduced.
*Definition*: introduces a term in terms of existing entries; adds nothing new.
*Convention*: a feature of the presentation, not a claim about what is described.
*Exclusion*: a view the commitments rule out as a precondition of registration.
*Presupposition*: assumed by the text without being stated as a commitment; to be examined.
*Open*: a question the layer raises and does not answer.
*Consequence*: follows from the entries it requires; recorded so that it can be cited, adds nothing new.
*Branch*: a further analysis compatible with every entry it builds on; kept open, not adopted.
*Closed*: an analysis that contradicts an entry; recorded with the entry it contradicts.
*Decision*: a choice between readings, with its reasons and whether it rests on a claim or on method.
*Objection*: an attack on an entry, with its current status.
*Friction*: anything that blocks progress or prompts revision, with its kind, the entries between
which it arises, and how it was resolved, if it was (see `organon/method/schema.md`).

Section numbers refer to *A Minimal Epistemic Core* (`latex/epistemic_core.tex`).

## Method (all layers)

The method is itself a set of assumptions. It is recorded here so that it can be examined and
revised like any other entry, and so that a result can be checked for features that come from the
method rather than from what it describes. It applies to every investigation in the repository;
test protocols are in `organon/method/`.

### Rules

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| M1 | Every result states whether it requires only the trunk (the entries that every analysis must satisfy) or a named branch. |
| M2 | A branch is closed when it contradicts an entry of the trunk, or can be kept only by readmitting an exclusion. Closing a branch does not affect results that do not require it. |
| M3 | Branches are not exclusive. They may be combined where they are consistent; some concern only one kind of domain. |
| M4 | When a branch is closed, record whether it was closed by a commitment about what is described or by a methodological presupposition (Mp-). A branch closed only by method is reopened if that presupposition is revised. |
| M5 | From time to time, rebuild a step under a different method (for instance, richer instead of minimal, or coherentist instead of foundational) and record which results survive. A result that survives several methods is less likely to be a feature of the method. |

### Methodological presuppositions

| Id | Presupposition | What it may cost |
|---|---|---|
| Mp-parsimony | Fewer commitments are preferred to more. This is a value of the method, not a claim about what is described. It contributed to the choice of Reading A. | Truths that require richer structure may be excluded for economy alone. |
| Mp-classical | Branches are closed by contradiction under classical logic. | A domain in which some contradictions hold would be closed off by the method. A branch that is consistent but false is never closed. |
| Mp-foundational | The theory is built upward from a trunk, each layer resting on those below. The alternative, that commitments support one another without a bottom layer (coherentism), has not been argued against. | Commitments of a lower layer cannot be revised in the light of a higher one without restructuring the register. |
| Mp-separable | Frame and content differ by role, not by kind. At any moment some entries function as frame (they are held fixed while others are examined) and others as content; the same entry can play either role, and content can force a change in what is held fixed. Each opener records what it holds fixed in `holds_fixed`. | No entry is protected by being method. A rule or presupposition can be refuted by what an investigation finds, and closures that rested on it (M4) must then be reopened. Conversely, nothing is examined without something else held fixed for the moment. |
| Mp-schema | The entry types, statuses, fields and link types of organon, as defined in method/schema.md and enforced by tools/check.py. Recorded as an entry so that frictions and revisions can name it. | Every fixed vocabulary is a set of differences supplied by the apparatus, not by what is recorded. Where a case does not fit, the vocabulary must be changed rather than the case forced. |

## Layer 1: the minimal epistemic core

### Question

| Id | Question | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Q0** | What preconditions enable knowledge, of any kind, prior to knowledge itself? | The author's formulation when the work began: "a minimal epistemological core is proposed (what preconditions enable knowledge, prior to knowledge itself)". The core claims necessary conditions only, not sufficient ones. |

### Premise

| Id | Statement | Notes | § |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P** | An epistemic relation is always a relation to something in particular. To perceive or claim anything about X, X must be distinguishable from what it is not, and that distinguishing must depend on X; otherwise what is perceived or claimed would not be about X. | Motivates D, R and C. The core claims necessity only: P yields necessary conditions, not sufficient ones. | 1 |

### Commitments

| Id | Statement | Requires | Does not establish | § |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **D** | *Differentiability.* F admits differentiation, although no particular differentiation is thereby realized or specified. | P | Any particular articulation, or its realization. | 2 |
| **R** | *Second relatum.* There is a second relatum R, distinct from F, that admits differentiation of its own. | P, D | A knowing subject, or any dependence on F. | 4 |
| **C** | *Receptive dependence.* Through C, the contrast of a specified articulation realized in F is matched by a contrast between conditions of R, and the latter contrast obtains partly in virtue of the former. | D, R, Df-articulation, Df-conditions | Which way F is; understanding, representation, order, acquisition, retention. | 5 |

Argument for **D** (§2): If every differentiation were supplied by the receiver, registering a difference in F could not be distinguished from the receiver's merely differing within itself, and by P what was registered would not be about F.

Argument for **R** (§4): A contrast in F and a contrast in a second relatum are not the same fact; without a differentiation of its own, nothing in R could distinguish registration from non-registration.

Argument for **C** (§5): D and R leave F and R unconnected; matching alone is symmetric (resemblance, correspondence), so registration needs an asymmetric dependence, which no description of the relata supplies.

### Definitions

| Id | Term | Definition | Requires | § |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Df-field | field F | Whatever is under consideration; fixes the scope of the inquiry. Implies no region, objects, boundary, or presentation to a subject. | none | 2 |
| Df-articulation | articulation ⟨a,δ,b⟩_F | A particular differentiation of F; a, b are its *terms*, δ its *contrast* (the respect in which the terms differ). Terms are positions, not prior objects. | D | 3 |
| Df-realized | realized articulation | F exhibits it: its terms are both actual and differ in δ. The terms are not alternatives. | Df-articulation | 3 |
| Df-specified | specified articulation | Its terms and contrast are fixed, by the account, not by F. Specification selects without creating, and can fail. | Df-articulation | 3 |
| Df-conditions | conditions r, r′ of R | The terms of a realized differentiation of R; both actual, co-present, neither alternatives nor stages. Need not share the form of an articulation of F. | R | 4 |
| Df-matching | matching | The terms of an articulation are paired with distinct conditions of R (a with r, b with r′). Symmetric. | Df-articulation, Df-conditions | 5 |
| Df-roles | target, receiver | In an instance of C: the target is the relatum whose contrast is depended upon; the receiver, the relatum whose contrast depends. Roles are positions in C, not natures of relata. | C | 5 |
| Df-registration | registration | A specified articulation realized in F is registered by R when C holds between them. Always registration *of* a specified articulation; an actual relation, not a disposition. | C, Df-specified, Df-realized | 6 |

### Conventions

| Id | Convention | § |
|---|---|---|
| Cv-two | Articulations are written with two terms; the account requires only at least two. | 3 |
| Cv-letters | F and R are named for the positions they occupy in the instances considered; nothing in R or C uses the notion of a receiver. | 5 |
| Cv-arrow | If C is written as an arrow, the same symbol must not also denote order. | 7 |
| Cv-figures | In figures, terms are marks, never areas; F and R are column headings, never enclosures; one arrow style is reserved for C; grey marks what belongs only to the theorist's description. | 3, 5, 6 |

### Exclusions (as preconditions of registration)

| Id | Excluded view | Excluded by | § |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | All differentiation is supplied by the receiver (pure constructivism). | D, P | 2 |
| E2 | Registration consists in resemblance or term-by-term correspondence. | C (second clause) | 5 |
| E3 | Registration is a transfer from target to receiver. | Df-registration | 6 |
| E4 | A repertoire of alternatives, in F, in R, or elsewhere, is a precondition of registration. | Df-realized, Df-conditions | 3, 6 |
| E5 | Time, or order of any kind, is a precondition of registration. | Df-registration (defined without order) | 7 |
| E6 | A knowing subject, concepts, or representations precede registration. | D, R, C (none involves them) | 4, 6 |

None of these denies that the excluded structures occur in particular epistemic relations; wherever
they are needed, they must enter as further commitments.

### Presuppositions (used but not yet stated as commitments)

These are assumed by the text of Layer 1 and are to be examined, accepted as commitments, or removed.

| Id | Presupposition | Where it appears | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ps-modal | "Admits" expresses a capacity of F (and of R) itself, not a stock of possibilities held anywhere. | D, R; §2 | unexamined |
| Ps-actual | Contrasts hold between actual terms only. | Df-realized, Df-conditions | unexamined |
| Ps-relata | Terms are positions within an articulation; whether relations are prior to relata, or the theory is neutral, is not settled. | Df-articulation; §3 | unexamined |
| Ps-ground | "In virtue of" is an asymmetric dependence that relates what actually obtains and need not be counterfactual; it is not analysed further. *Examined in Layer 2: replaced by C-prim, C-asym, C-actual, C-partial, C-kind.* | C; §5 | examined |
| Ps-individ | Enough individuation to distinguish F from R and to take r, r′ as conditions of one relatum; no more. | R; §4 | unexamined |
| Ps-logic | The exposition uses identity, distinction, relation, and inference without attributing them to what it describes. | §1 | unexamined |

### Open questions

| Id | Question | § |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | What grounds the asymmetry of C in a given domain? | 5, 8 |
| Q2 | Can receptive dependence be explained in terms of more elementary relations? *Layer 2 leaves C unanalysed; the open branches B-power, B-ground, B-cause, B-reg are the candidate answers.* | 8 |
| Q3 | Can registration of *which way* F is be reconstructed from contrasts between actual terms, without admitting alternatives? | 6, 8 |
| Q4 | What order do acquisition and retention require, and is anything stronger than an asymmetric relation needed? | 7, 8 |

### Decisions

| Id | Decision | Reasons | Basis (M4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dec-readingA | *Reading A.* Contrasts hold only between actual, co-present terms; the core admits no repertoire of alternatives (Reading A), rather than contrasts between an actual term and its alternatives (Reading B). | In the author's words: "Must be A. B needs some sort of alternative repository or other metaphysical assumptions we do not want to make." The reason is partly about content (an alternative must be held somewhere, which the core does not supply) and partly methodological (Mp-parsimony). Recorded under M4 as resting on both. | both |

## Layer 2: ontology of the core

This layer examines the presuppositions of Layer 1, taking a position only where the core forces one.
It has no paper yet; § refers to the passage of Layer 1 it reads.

Layer 2 does not choose among analyses of the core's notions. It states what every analysis must
satisfy (the *trunk*) and keeps each compatible analysis open as a *branch*, following the rules
M1–M5 under **Method** above.

### The dependence in C: trunk

| Id | Kind | Statement | Requires | § |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-prim | Commitment | The dependence named by "in virtue of" in C is primitive: the core characterizes it by C-asym, C-actual and C-partial, and does not analyse it further. | C | 5 |
| C-asym | Commitment | *Asymmetry.* If one contrast obtains partly in virtue of another, the second does not obtain in virtue of the first. The asymmetry holds between contrasts, not between relata: F and R may each depend on the other in different respects. | C, Df-roles | 5 |
| C-actual | Commitment | *Actuality.* C relates two contrasts that both obtain. It says nothing about what would obtain otherwise. | C, Ps-actual | 5 |
| C-partial | Commitment | *Partiality.* The receiving contrast obtains partly in virtue of the target contrast; the remainder is supplied by the organization of R. | C | 5 |
| C-kind | Commitment | *Kind-neutrality.* The core requires that C obtain, not that it be of one kind. What the dependence consists in (causal, constitutive, logical, or other) is fixed in each domain, if at all. | C-prim | 5 |
| C-local | Consequence | Whether C obtains in an instance is not fixed by descriptions of the relata, nor by what would obtain otherwise. Two instances alike in their relata and in their matching may therefore differ in whether C obtains: one is registration, the other mere correspondence (Figure 2b). | C, C-actual, E2 | 5 |

C-local leaves one question open: whether C in an instance can depend on *other actual instances*,
as in a pattern across cases. Reading A excludes alternatives, which are non-actual; other instances
are actual, so Reading A does not settle this. B-single and B-reg below answer it in opposite ways.

### The dependence in C: branches

| Id | Analysis | Adds | Compatible because | Closed if |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B-single | *Singularity.* Whether C obtains is a fact about the instance alone. | Nothing beyond the instance; denies B-reg. | It requires no entity beyond the two contrasts. | Some later result needs C to be fixed by cases beyond the instance. |
| B-reg | *Regularity.* C obtains in an instance in virtue of a pattern across actual instances. | Other instances as a precondition of registration. | The instances are actual, so no alternative is admitted. | The pattern can be stated only over possible cases (E4), or fixes no direction (E2). |
| B-power | *Capacities.* C is the exercise of a receptive capacity of R, prompted by the contrast in F. | Capacities as constituents of relata. Settles Ps-modal: "admits" names a capacity. Explains C-partial: R's capacity is the remainder. | A capacity can be exercised in an actual instance. | A capacity can be identified only by what it would do in non-actual circumstances (E4, C-actual); or no sense can be given to capacities in non-physical domains (C-kind). |
| B-ground | *Constitution.* In some domains, the receiving contrast is partially grounded in the target contrast. | A domain-specific kind of C. | Ground relates facts, is asymmetric, holds between what actually obtains, and admits a partial form. | Ground requires the grounded to be nothing over and above its ground, against R being distinct from F; or its necessitation can be stated only over non-actual cases (C-actual). |
| B-cause | *Causation.* In physical domains, C is causal dependence. | A domain-specific kind of C. | Causation can be taken as asymmetric, actual and partial. | C is taken to consist in a transfer from F to R (E3). |

### The dependence in C: closed

| Id | Analysis | Contradicts | Closed by (M4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| X-cf | C holds because R would differ if F differed (counterfactual or interventionist dependence). | C-actual, E4: it requires non-actual cases. | Commitment; but Reading A, on which C-actual and E4 rest, was adopted partly on Mp-parsimony. |
| X-rule | C is a rule assigning conditions of R to terms of F. | Restricted to actual terms, a rule is only the pairing a with r, b with r′, which is matching (E2); anything more concerns values not taken (E4). | Commitment (E2); the second half also rests on Reading A. |
| X-transfer | C consists in something passing from F to R. | E3. | Commitment. |

Closed analyses are closed *as analyses of C*. As in Layer 1, the structures they describe may enter
later layers as further commitments.

### Decisions

| Id | Decision | Reasons | Basis (M4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dec-trunk | *Trunk and branches for C.* Keep the dependence in C primitive (C-prim) and characterize it by its properties, instead of choosing one analysis of it; keep every compatible analysis open as a branch. | The author's image: at the base of a tree we know the trunk, roots and branches, but not where the fruit is; a conflict may show only far along a branch. A primitive with stated properties is not a rival to the analyses but what they share, so keeping it primitive keeps the branches open. Claude had first recommended choosing generic dependence over capacities; the author asked why one must choose, and the answer is that one need not. | method |

### Proposals

| Id | Proposal | Open | By | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lead-repertoire | *Alternatives as actual conditions of the receiver.* Registration of which way F is may need no non-actual alternatives, if the alternatives are actual conditions of R. A receiver can have an actual, co-present differentiation into many conditions (as organon has a list of statuses); registering which way F is would be: which of R's actual conditions answers, through C, to the term realized in F. The other conditions are actual too, but nothing in F answers to them. | Whether this says which way F is, or only which way R is: the unoccupied conditions are actual in R, but their relevance to F seems to be exactly what alternatives supplied. If that relevance can be stated without modality, F-which closes within Reading A. | claude | proposed |

### Objections

| Id | Objection | Attacks | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Obj-stroud | *Stroud's objection.* The core argues from P to its necessary conditions, which is the form of a transcendental argument. Stroud argued that such arguments establish at most what must be believed, or how things must seem, not how things are. Applied here: D, R and C might be necessary for registration *by receivers like us*, not "of any kind". | P | open |

### Tests

The first result expected to separate the branches is Q3: whether registration of *which way* F is
can be reconstructed from contrasts between actual terms. A branch that answers Q3 without
readmitting alternatives gains; one that can answer it only by readmitting them is closed by M2.

### Still to examine

Ps-modal (in part answered by B-power), Ps-relata, Ps-individ, Ps-logic.

### Literature

Records checked on 2026-10-23, texts not yet read for this layer: Anscombe, *Causality and
Determination* (1971), for singular causation (B-single, B-cause); Mumford and Anjum, *Getting Causes
from Powers* (2011), for B-power; Fine, "Guide to Ground" (2012), and Bennett, *Making Things Up*
(2017), for B-ground and for dependence as a generic notion with kinds (C-kind); Stroud,
"Transcendental Arguments" (1968), for Obj-stroud. Keys in `organon/library/refs.bib`.

## Frictions (all layers)

| Id | Friction | Kind | Between | Effect | Status | Resolution | Resolved by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-readings | *Two readings of contrast.* The first draft could be read two ways: a contrast holds between co-present actual terms (Reading A), or between an actual term and its alternatives (Reading B). The arguments of the core went through on one reading and not the other. | ambiguity | Df-articulation | blocks | resolved | reject | Dec-readingA |
| F-time | *Time claimed necessary.* Draft-time claims more than P supports: P yields necessary conditions, and nothing in it requires time rather than some weaker order. | overreach | Draft-time, P | prompts | resolved | restrict | E5, Q4 |
| F-collapse | *Registration collapsing into matching.* With matching alone, registration cannot be told apart from resemblance or correspondence: the distinction the core needs disappears. | collapse | Df-matching, Df-registration | prompts | resolved | distinguish | C, E2 |
| F-cf | *Counterfactual analysis of C.* A counterfactual analysis of C requires non-actual cases; C-actual says C relates only contrasts that hold. | contradiction | X-cf, C-actual | prompts | resolved | reject | X-cf |
| F-ground | *Ground and distinct relata.* On standard accounts, what is grounded is nothing over and above its ground. R is distinct from F. B-ground can be kept only if partial ground between facts about distinct relata is coherent. | tension | B-ground, R | prompts | open |  |  |
| F-single | *Singularity or regularity.* Both branches are compatible with everything so far: nothing yet decides whether C in an instance is fixed by the instance alone or by a pattern across actual instances. | underdetermination | B-single, B-reg | prompts | open |  |  |
| F-which | *Which way F is.* Registration as defined is of a specified articulation. Later layers need registration of *which way* F is, and under Reading A this must be reconstructed from contrasts between actual terms, without alternatives. Until it is, the epistemic apparatus cannot be built on the core (Q3). | gap | Df-registration, Dec-readingA | blocks | open |  |  |
| F-trivial | *Primitive dependence may be empty.* Characterized only as asymmetric, actual and partial, the primitive dependence may say too little: many relations have these properties. If no instance can be shown to differ from correspondence by C alone (and C-local says no description fixes it), C-prim risks being a name for the difference rather than an account of it. | triviality | C-prim | prompts | open |  |  |

### Withdrawn claims

| Id | Claim | Why withdrawn |
|---|---|---|
| Draft-time | *Registration requires time.* Registration, or at least the acquisition and retention built on it, requires time. | Raised in the review of the first draft. The author objected that time is a loaded notion and that claiming it necessary overreaches: structures that are ordered but not temporal may suffice. The core keeps only an asymmetric relation, with transitivity left open (E5, Q4). See F-time. |
